tier_reason: Independent third-party shootout (r-lyeh-archived/scriptorium, 525 stars) with public harness (bench.cc, run.bat, tests/fib.as, per-engine make.bat) lists AngelScript 2.039 s against Duktape 9.544 s and PUC Lua 1.341 s. Compiler is ambiguous (VS2015 RC or VS2013) and the CPU is only 'AMD A10 3.8 GHz', so it falls short of A.

corrections.baseline: Duktape 1.2.2 (javascript/duktape/duktape.h in the scriptorium tree); the same table lists PUC Lua 5.3.1 at 1.341 s, where this engine is slower
corrections.compiler_and_flags: MSVC, VS2015 RC where possible and VS2013 otherwise (which one per engine is not stated); per-engine make.bat: AngelScript 2.29.2 built with cl /Ox /Oy /MT /DNDEBUG /EHsc /DAS_USE_STLNAMES=1, Duktape built with cl /Ox /Oy /MT /DNDEBUG
corrections.workload: Recursive fibonacci test (tests/fib.as, tests/fib.js, tests/fib.lua) run as a separate process through the repo's bench.exe ('bench 5 ...' in run.bat), wall time including process start-up averaged over 5 runs; AngelScript 2.29.2 versus Duktape 1.2.2 and Lua 5.3.1, July 2015 snapshot.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 286 stars, 58 forks; packaged as vcpkg port 'angelscript' (2.38.0) and Conan Center recipe 'angelscript' (2.38.0)
corrections.caveats: Eleven-year-old snapshot (July 2015) of AngelScript 2.29.2 against Duktape 1.2.2 on one recursive-fib test; the author says 'Take it with a grain of salt'. Timings include process start-up and vary between logged runs (bench.csv shows Duktape from 9.06 s to 14.3 s and AngelScript 2.04 to 2.08 s). Both engines are many releases old. AngelScript loses to the main embedded-scripting incumbent: PUC Lua 5.3.1 is faster in the same table (1.341 s versus 2.039 s, about 1.5x, derived from page data), so the only baseline it beats is Duktape. Scriptorium is an archived repository; per-engine flags are in each make.bat (/Ox /Oy /MT /DNDEBUG) but the CPU model is not exact and the VS2013/VS2015 choice per engine is not stated. The 1.859 s 'angelscript-jit' row is the separate BlindMindStudios AngelScript-JIT-Compiler, not this repository. A separate April 2026 benchmark (sashi0034/script-language-benchmark, Windows, Visual Studio 17 2022 Release; the author notes the code was generated with Codex and not fully reviewed) has AngelScript faster than Lua on 7 of 16 workloads (float2string, mandelbrot, native_loop by 0.3%, particles_kinematics, queen, sha256, spectral_norm) and slower on 9 (for example dictionary 20.888 versus 4.025, sort 328.950 versus 6.175, fibonacci_recursive 795.218 versus 599.702); units are not stated.

notes: Numbers verified on the scriptorium README and bench.csv; licence (Zlib, LICENSE.md), last commit 2026-10-05 and vcpkg/Conan packaging confirmed. Main shortcoming: slower than PUC Lua (1.341 s vs 2.039 s) and only faster than an old Duktape 1.2.2 on a 2015 single fib test; caveat corrected because per-engine flags do exist in make.bat.

tier_reason: Independent third-party CI shootout (ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark, v8-v7 suite forked from mozilla/arewefastyet) lists bare 41468/40758/36041 against QuickJS 1217/1761/1067 and Duktape 489/905/371 on ubuntu/macos-arm64/windows. Code is public but compiler flags and CPU model are not stated (GitHub-hosted runners, bare built with default bare-make settings), so not A; same tier as the verified V8, ChakraCore and Ant entries from this suite.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Built by ahaoboy/bare-build build.sh: shallow clone of holepunchto/bare, 'bare-make generate --no-cache' and 'bare-make build' with default settings; compiler and flags not stated
corrections.stars_or_usage: 1.2k stars, 35 forks; benchmark suite ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark has 59 stars
corrections.caveats: A JIT engine against interpreters: Bare runs V8 through libjs ('low-level bindings to V8 in an engine independent manner'), so the win over QuickJS and Duktape is V8's JIT, not Bare's own code. In the same table the plain V8 shell scores higher (ubuntu 48107, macos-arm64 64220, windows 46932) and Node is close (40333 on ubuntu), so Bare adds no speed over the already-verified V8 entry; it is a V8 embedding runtime and a duplicate candidate of that entry. Third-party CI suite (59 stars) on GitHub-hosted runners without stated flags or CPU model; Bare's version cell on the page is empty (built from the main branch with default bare-make settings). Large footprint: 64.6M on ubuntu versus 1M for QuickJS (Score/MB 642 versus 1190). Ratios over Duktape (about 85x ubuntu, 45x macos-arm64, 97x windows, derived from page data) compare against Duktape 2.99.99/2.7.0 interpreters.

notes: All scores verified on the suite README (results dated 10/5/2026); Apache-2.0, 1.2k stars, last commit 2026-10-06 confirmed. Main shortcoming: speed is V8's (Bare scores below the plain V8 shell in the same table), so the orchestrator may want decision 'duplicate' against https://github.com/v8/v8 (wrapper/runtime of an already-listed engine).

tier_reason: Independent third-party shootout (drujensen/fib, 906 stars) with public code (fib.scm, fib.lua, run.sh, Dockerfile) lists 'guile fib.scm' at 102.887 s against 'lua fib.lua' at 203.702 s. Interpreter build flags are not stated and the CPU is only 'Intel Xeon 3.1Ghz', so not A.

corrections.workload: Naive recursive fibonacci fib(47) = 2,971,215,073, run as 'guile fib.scm' and 'lua fib.lua' and timed with bash 'time' (whole process, start-up included), average of 5 runs, last run 2024-12-05.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Guile installed from the apt package guile-3.0 and Lua 5.4.7 through asdf in an amd64/ubuntu:24.04 Docker image (versions table: guile 3.0.10, lua 5.4.7); the README states only common release flags for compiled languages and gives none for the interpreters
corrections.caveats: Single naive-recursion micro-benchmark, so it says little about general scripting workloads; last run 2024-12-05. Guile 3 has a JIT (NEWS: 'Just-in-time code generation') and auto-compiles the script to bytecode, while PUC Lua is a pure interpreter; the page files Guile under 'Interpreted'. LuaJIT 2.1.1 (37.837 s) is far faster than both. Whole-process wall time with bash 'time'. The repo URL is a stale unofficial GitHub mirror (0 stars, last commit 2022-04-08); upstream moved to codeberg.org/guile/guile.git and released Guile 3.0.11 in December 2025 (search snippet only, codeberg and gnu.org not reachable here), so the project is active but its last commit date could not be checked. Benchmark code and Dockerfile are public but the CPU model is only 'Intel Xeon 3.1Ghz'.

notes: Numbers verified on drujensen/fib README; licence LGPL-3.0-or-later confirmed from the mirror's LICENSE file. Main shortcoming: one fib micro-benchmark and a stale mirror URL (canonical repo codeberg.org/guile/guile per search snippet); maintenance_status set to active from the 3.0.11 release in December 2025 (snippet only), last_commit left as the mirror's date.
